reason: The liners need support to become growing beds, and the metal stock seems suited to making frames for them.
expectation: I expect to make supported bed containers, though they may still need a growing medium.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the bricks might provide a growing medium, but I want to prepare the beds first.

effect: The troughs now have supported liners and separate lower reservoirs, so I can turn to preparing material for the beds.
reaction: It is satisfying to see how the metal braces support the wet liners.
reason: Breaking the porous bricks may produce material suitable for the growing beds.
expectation: I expect the hammer to break the bricks into smaller pieces, though I do not yet know whether they will need further preparation.

alternatives.reason: The plants will likely need nutrients, but I want to prepare the bed material first.

effect: The crushed bricks need washing and a leach check before they can go near the roots, so preparing the granules is the next priority.
reaction: The leach check is an interesting reminder that a growing medium needs more than a useful texture.
reason: The wash and test bench directly matches the preparation the granules need.
expectation: I expect the granules to be washed and checked for substances that could leach out, though I do not know the result.

alternatives.reason: Nutrient solution will likely be useful, but the granules need checking first.

effect: The granules passed the leach check and can support roots, but they will need a separate nutrient supply.
reaction: I like the distinction between a medium that supports roots and one that feeds them.
reason: Putting the clean granules into the lined troughs seems like the next step toward a usable growing bed.
expectation: I expect the troughs to be filled with the clean granules, though they may still need water and nutrients.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution also seems necessary, but I want to prepare the beds first.

effect: The clean granules are now in the lined troughs, so the beds still need water and nutrients.
reaction: The assembly followed as expected; nothing notable.
reason: Mixing drinking water with nutrient concentrate seems like a practical way to supply the roots.
expectation: I expect to make a nutrient solution for the troughs, though I do not know how it will reach the roots.

alternatives.reason: The bricks and metal might make another useful structure, but their purpose is less clear to me.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to add to the prepared troughs.
reaction: The mixture came together as expected; nothing notable.
reason: Combining the solution with the troughs should supply the roots with water and nutrients.
expectation: I expect the troughs to receive the nutrient solution, though I am unsure how they will also provide enough air to the roots.

alternatives.reason: The bricks and metal may make a useful structure, but adding the solution has a clearer purpose now.

effect: The solution drains through the granules into reservoirs, leaving air around the roots while circulation returns the water. The chapter is complete.
reaction: The explanation of how drainage supplies air resolved my uncertainty and made the trough design more interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: I found irrigating the troughs most worthwhile because the result explained how drainage and circulation give roots both water and air.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the troughs was straightforward and produced no further explanation, so it stood out least to me.

surprise.text: I had not expected the troughs to have separate reservoirs and circulation fittings that return the water.

arbitrary.text: The offered combination of fired bricks and metal stock had no clear purpose for me, though I did not try it. The actions I chose had understandable purposes.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the practical details about testing the granules and supplying roots with air made me curious about what comes next.
